workLog.action: Mirrored the canonical pytest.yml job contract
workLog.result: yaml.safe_load confirmed two jobs both named Run Python Tests: test (line 111) owning the Run pytest step (line 260) and skip-tests (line 427) owning the skip step (line 441). A name match alone cannot decide a verdict, so classification is by step name.

Stdlib-only resolver. Validates a 40-hex expected head, re-reads the live head from refs/pull/N/head, rejects stale heads and push runs, picks the latest run attempt, classifies executor versus pass-through jobs by step name, applies worst-wins severity across duplicate job names, and returns PASS, FAIL, SKIPPED, PENDING, STALE, CANCELLED, or UNKNOWN with a fixed-vocabulary reason. Argv-list subprocess calls, no shell.

workLog.action: Verified the resolver against live GitHub API payloads
workLog.result: Run 31360441685 reports run conclusion success with both Run Python Tests jobs success, yet the suite never ran; the resolver returns SKIPPED where a conclusion read would have returned PASS. Runs 31355229018, 31362376502, 31361938848, and 31360447277 resolve to PASS, CANCELLED, PENDING, and UNKNOWN respectively. End-to-end run against PR 4819 returned PASS with agreement AGREE.

57 tests covering stale head, push rejection, latest attempt, sibling failure wins, pass-through-only SKIPPED, pending, no run, cancelled, 403, malformed data, output sanitation, and the CLI contract. Includes a regression pin built from the real green-but-unrun payload.

One step appended to run-tests plus actions: read on that job. Existing outputs, step names, and check names are unchanged; the authoritative duplicate pytest run still executes. continue-on-error and an unconditional exit 0 keep the shadow step from changing any verdict.

workLog.action: Review finding 1: closed sibling failure masking in aggregate()
workLog.result: aggregate() returned inside the tier loop, so the first non-empty tier decided outright and an executor PASS or SKIPPED masked a lower-tier FAIL. The deciding tier now sets a base verdict and every lower-tier status outside BENIGN_SIBLING_STATUSES escalates it through worst(). Escalation is downward only because all jobs carry the same required check name, so an unhealthy sibling means that check is not green whatever the executor observed. PASS, SKIPPED and UNKNOWN stay benign: UNKNOWN so a failure to classify cannot erase a directly observed PASS, and SKIPPED because pytest.yml ships a real skip-tests job with empty steps, so escalating it would turn every ordinary green PR into SKIPPED. That inverse is pinned by test_a_benign_sibling_does_not_disturb_an_executor_pass and by a dedicated mutant. Two dead fallbacks were removed once every job was shown to classify into exactly one of three tiers.

workLog.action: Review finding 2: bound candidate runs to the requested pull request
workLog.result: Runs were matched on head SHA alone, and a SHA can head more than one PR, so another PR's run could supply the verdict. binds_to_pr() now requires the number in the run pull_requests array, falling back to comparing head_repository.full_name against the already validated repository constant when GitHub omits the list. Live reads on 2026-08-10 proved that omission is normal rather than anomalous: open PRs 4832, 4833, 4834 and 4817 each carry their own number while every run of merged PR 4819 carries an empty list, so treating empty as failure would break the resolver on closed PRs. The fallback is a comparison against a trusted constant, never an ingestion, and a fork cannot match the upstream full name. Runs that match the SHA but bind to nothing now resolve UNKNOWN with REASON_RUN_NOT_BOUND, distinct from PENDING for no run at all. Proven on a real payload: the run for PR 4833 binds as 4833 and is rejected as 4834.

workLog.action: Review finding 3: made the shadow observable rather than silent
workLog.result: A shadow that speaks only on disagreement cannot be told apart from a dead one. emit() now prints exactly one greppable ::notice::shadow-pytest-sample line on every invocation carrying status, agreement and compared, exposes shadow_pytest_compared as a fourth output for sample counting, and warns when no sample was collected. The workflow step condition moved to !cancelled() so a failing local pytest run still yields a sample while a cancelled job spends no API calls.

workLog.action: Extended the mutation harness from 9 to 18 mutants and found a real gap
workLog.result: All 17 real mutants DEAD, control SURVIVED, restore byte-identical. The harness requires each needle to occur exactly once, which caught a genuine hole: the raw-agreement-reason mutant stopped applying once liveness gave its target two call sites, and splitting it per branch showed the sanitizer on the no-sample warning was unobserved. A mutant against that branch survived until test_the_no_sample_warning_sanitizes_the_reason_it_is_handed was added.

workLog.action: Validated the review fixes and committed as 9a0f4ce7
workLog.result: 83 focused tests pass, up from 57. 637 pass across tests/quality_gate/ and tests/workflows/. pre_pr.py exits 0, which included fixing two mypy union-attr errors the ratchet caught in the test file: tests are type-checked even though mypy reports tests.* as an unused section. A usable_scan() helper now returns a non-optional RunScan and fails by name, leaving scan_runs() for the one test that asserts the None path. taste count ratchet 581 against baseline 583, unchanged. actionlint exit 0, yamllint adds no new warning. Three files changed, still five authored files total.

workLog.action: Simplified both authored files under the 500-line taste-lints gate, committed as 0e88151e
workLog.result: The resolver fell from 729 to 494 lines and its tests from 988 to 491, clearing the two file-size errors that were blocking the build. The file budget forbade a sixth file, so the fix was deletion, not extraction: a 125-line module docstring that restated the workflow, three single-caller wrappers inlined into their only callers, four near-identical status functions collapsed into job_status(job, kind) driven by the _GREEN_STATUS table whose insertion order already encoded the tier order, gh_json returning the payload or None instead of a pair the callers re-validated, and the RunScan container, worst(), build_parser() and __all__ deleted. In the tests, repeated GhFake literals became one gh_stub() and families of one-line tests became dict-driven parametrize tables, which is why 83 cases survive a 497-line cut.

workLog.action: Proved the simplification changed no behaviour
workLog.result: A differential harness loaded the pre-change and post-change modules side by side and compared status, reason, stdout, stderr and every output key across 24 API scenarios by 5 local statuses, plus main() over 6 argument vectors: zero differences, and --help is byte-identical. A 20-mutant battery covering the whole contract (stale head, push filter, head SHA, PR binding, fork rejection, run and attempt selection, the skipped pytest step, pass-through tiering, incomplete jobs, tier precedence, sibling escalation and its benign inverse, unrecognised conclusions, unbound runs, the job-name filter, sanitation, config exit, and both unreadable-payload guards) killed all 20 from a clean tree. Cohesion stays 1.0: that score is a function of file length and definition count, so only splitting the module can move it.
